questions.q: What, according to the article, happens in a society that curbs freedom of expression?
options: People turn to study instead
Not quite. The article says: People go on thinking but hide their thoughts, so the society fills with hypocrisy and creativity dries up.
People become more united
Not quite. The article says: People go on thinking but hide their thoughts, so the society fills with hypocrisy and creativity dries up.
People stop thinking altogether
Not quite. The article says: People go on thinking but hide their thoughts, so the society fills with hypocrisy and creativity dries up.
People go on thinking but hide their thoughts, so the society fills with hypocrisy and creativity dries up
Yes. Thinking cannot be stopped; only honesty is.
questions.rationale: “If curbs are placed on freedom of expression, people’s thinking cannot be stopped, the only thing that will take place is that their thinking will not come to their lips and pens.”

questions.q: “May God bless the man who sends me the gift of my own shortcoming.” What quality of a believer do these words of Umar express?
options: Eagerness to have his errors pointed out, so that he may correct them
Right. Accepting truth at the cost of prestige is called the greatest worship.
A wish to find fault with others
Not quite. The article says: Eagerness to have his errors pointed out, so that he may correct them.
Patience with those who flatter him
Not quite. The article says: Eagerness to have his errors pointed out, so that he may correct them.
Indifference to what people say
Not quite. The article says: Eagerness to have his errors pointed out, so that he may correct them.
questions.rationale: “The highest point of this attribute is that man is always prepared, rather he eagerly waits for someone to point out to him any shortcoming of his.”

questions.q: How does belief in the oneness of God shape a person’s character, according to the article?
options: It makes him anxious about the future
Not quite. The article says: It makes him humble before God, yet gives him dignity, confidence and respect for all as equals.
It makes him withdraw from other people
Not quite. The article says: It makes him humble before God, yet gives him dignity, confidence and respect for all as equals.
It makes him proud of his knowledge
Not quite. The article says: It makes him humble before God, yet gives him dignity, confidence and respect for all as equals.
It makes him humble before God, yet gives him dignity, confidence and respect for all as equals
Well read. Submission and freedom together.
questions.rationale: “Belief in Tawheed makes a person humble and modest… Submission to one God results in individual freedom and dignity, for, all human beings become equal.”

questions.q: Differences between people are inevitable. What does the article ask of someone who has a goal in life?
options: To give up the goal when opposed
Not quite. The article says: Not to let differences grow into conflict, and to stay focused on the work.
To remove everyone who differs
Not quite. The article says: Not to let differences grow into conflict, and to stay focused on the work.
To settle every difference by debate first
Not quite. The article says: Not to let differences grow into conflict, and to stay focused on the work.
Not to let differences grow into conflict, and to stay focused on the work
Correct. Friction wastes the effort the goal needs.
questions.rationale: “While carrying out of his goals, he should not allow differences to escalate into conflict.”

questions.q: What does the article say is special about a believer’s prayer in a time of trial?
options: It follows a fixed wording exactly
Not quite. The article says: It comes in new, heartfelt words he had not known before, born of discovering his helplessness.
It is said together with many people
Not quite. The article says: It comes in new, heartfelt words he had not known before, born of discovering his helplessness.
It comes in new, heartfelt words he had not known before, born of discovering his helplessness
Yes. Not formal, oft-repeated phrases.
It is longer than at other times
Not quite. The article says: It comes in new, heartfelt words he had not known before, born of discovering his helplessness.
questions.rationale: “It is not the formal duas and oft-repeated recitations that appear on his tongue, rather these are original and new supplications.”

questions.article: Freedom of Expression and Dissent in Islam
questions.q: Caliph Umar announced a limit on dowers, and an old woman objected, citing the Quran. How did he respond?
options: He ordered her to be silent
Not quite. The article says: He accepted her correction openly.
He accepted her correction openly
Right. “A woman has quarreled with Umar and has bested him.”
He asked the scholars to answer her
Not quite. The article says: He accepted her correction openly.
He promised to consider it later
Not quite. The article says: He accepted her correction openly.
questions.rationale: According to another account, Umar said: “May God forgive me, everyone knows better than Umar, even this old lady.”

questions.q: Why does the article call prayer “the ultimate degree of realism” rather than wishful thinking?
options: Because it follows fixed timings
Not quite. The article says: It acknowledges things as they are: man’s complete dependence and God’s absolute power.
Because it is practised by many people
Not quite. The article says: It acknowledges things as they are: man’s complete dependence and God’s absolute power.
Because prayers are always answered at once
Not quite. The article says: It acknowledges things as they are: man’s complete dependence and God’s absolute power.
It acknowledges things as they are: man’s complete dependence and God’s absolute power
Well reasoned. Prayer puts us in our true place.
questions.rationale: “Prayer, then, is not the wishful thinking or illusions of the pious but is actually acceptance of things as they are.”

questions.q: A writer who studied great men found two qualities common to them all. Which?
options: Physical strength and good health
Not quite. The article says: Curiosity and discontent – never satisfied with second best.
Wealth and good connections
Not quite. The article says: Curiosity and discontent – never satisfied with second best.
Curiosity and discontent – never satisfied with second best
Yes. These kept them striving higher.
Caution and contentment
Not quite. The article says: Curiosity and discontent – never satisfied with second best.
questions.rationale: “All of the men he had studied had been filled with curiosity and discontent.”

questions.q: The article says ablution (wudu) before each of the five daily prayers amounts to what?
options: A symbolic act with no cleansing value
Not quite. The article says: A half-bath five times a day – showing how central cleanliness is to faith.
A half-bath five times a day – showing how central cleanliness is to faith
Correct. “Keeping oneself clean is one half of faith.”
A practice meant only for Fridays
Not quite. The article says: A half-bath five times a day – showing how central cleanliness is to faith.
A custom for travellers
Not quite. The article says: A half-bath five times a day – showing how central cleanliness is to faith.
questions.rationale: “As a cleansing process, wudu is the equivalent of a half-bath. In this way, the devout Muslim takes a half-bath five times daily.”

questions.q: At the end of prayer the worshipper turns right and left saying “Peace and blessings of God be upon you.” What does the article see in this?
options: A daily lesson in wishing well to the whole world
Exactly. God is “Lord of the worlds,” not of one people.
A sign that the prayer was too long
Not quite. The article says: A daily lesson in wishing well to the whole world.
A farewell to the mosque
Not quite. The article says: A daily lesson in wishing well to the whole world.
A greeting meant only for those praying alongside
Not quite. The article says: A daily lesson in wishing well to the whole world.
questions.rationale: “One of the aims of salath (prayers) is to instill in believers, feelings of well-wishing for the whole world.”
